walkthroughs.body_html:
Language, Thought and Communication — a core area of GCSE Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Language, Thought and Communication brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Language, Thought and Communication.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The hypothesis that language shapes thought is named after:
options: Piaget and Vygotsky
Sapir and Whorf
Skinner and Watson
Chomsky and Pinker

mcqs.q: Whose bee waggle dance research showed animal signalling?
options: Lorenz
Tinbergen
Von Frisch
Harlow
They block all neurotransmitters.
Every member of the target population has an equal chance of selection.
Just grabbing whoever is around (any haphazard method).
Picking participants who match the population profile.
